findings.summary: 3D projection is a design technique that maps three-dimensional object points onto a two-dimensional plane using visual perspective and geometric analysis. It preserves conceptual solidity on flat surfaces, commonly applied in engineering, drafting, and computer graphics. Transformations are calculated via projection matrices, parallel projection, or perspective projection, each relying on axonometric or optical methods to handle depth and foreshortening.

mechanisms.title: Parallel projection
mechanisms.explanation: Parallel projection preserves line parallelism by projecting along parallel lines of sight, either orthographically (perpendicular rays) or obliquely (angled rays). It is used for working drawings and technical drafting where size and shape must remain undistorted by the object's position relative to the projection plane.

mechanisms.title: Perspective projection
mechanisms.explanation: Perspective projection preserves the 3D appearance by applying scaling and translation based on the object's relative position to the 2D surface. It uses a finite focal length to simulate how objects appear smaller with distance, enabling depth perception on flat displays through foreshortening and vanishing points.
